note: Gutenberg is the WordPress block editor as a Drupal @Editor + @Filter on a 'gutenberg' text format, enabled PER CONTENT TYPE. The 'Enable Gutenberg experience' checkbox on the content-type form writes gutenberg.settings:<node_type>_enable_full = true (read by GutenbergContentTypeManager::isContentTypeSupported). Sibling keys: <type>_template, <type>_template_lock, <type>_allowed_image_styles. Blocks are discovered from the module's gutenberg.blocks.yml plus any MODULE.gutenberg.yml (libraries-edit/libraries-view/dynamic-blocks/custom-blocks); editor JS plugins are a real plugin type (@GutenbergPlugin, manager plugin.manager.gutenberg.plugin, e.g. DrupalImage). Field formatter gutenberg_text. Permissions: use gutenberg, manage blocks lock, create and edit custom gutenberg content blocks. Introspection reads gutenberg.settings for a namespaced content type; execution enables Gutenberg on a content type and sets a template lock, both verified against live gutenberg.settings config. Evals ground in the text-format/editor config and per-content-type enablement, not the browser JS.

evals.prompt: How do you turn the Gutenberg editor on for a Drupal content type, and where is that choice stored? There is no global settings page.
evals.expected_output: On the content type's add/edit form tick 'Enable Gutenberg experience'; this stores gutenberg.settings:<node_type>_enable_full = true (read by GutenbergContentTypeManager::isContentTypeSupported). There is no configure route (configure=null).

evals.prompt: Which text format and editor does the Gutenberg module ship, and what plugin ids implement the editor and filter?
evals.expected_output: It ships the 'gutenberg' text format (filter.format.gutenberg, 'Gutenberg Blocks text format') paired with editor.editor.gutenberg. The Editor plugin id is 'gutenberg' and the Filter plugin id is 'gutenberg' (a required TYPE_TRANSFORM_REVERSIBLE filter). It also provides the gutenberg_text field formatter.

evals.prompt: How can a module or theme register its own Gutenberg editor blocks, and how are editor JS plugins added?
evals.expected_output: Provide a MODULE.gutenberg.yml (or THEME.gutenberg.yml) discovery file with libraries-edit, libraries-view, dynamic-blocks and custom-blocks sections (discovered by GutenbergLibraryManager/BlocksLibraryManager). Editor JS plugins are a plugin type: @GutenbergPlugin (manager plugin.manager.gutenberg.plugin, namespace Plugin/GutenbergPlugin, base GutenbergPluginBase), e.g. DrupalImage.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, exactly one content type has the Gutenberg editor enabled. Inspect the live gutenberg configuration and give the machine name of that content type.
On this Drupal site, the Gutenberg-enabled content type 'gutenberg_probe' has a block template lock configured. Inspect the live gutenberg configuration and state the template lock mode.
On this Drupal site there is a content type with machine name 'gutenberg_task'. Enable the Gutenberg editor experience for it, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: gutenberg.settings:gutenberg_task_enable_full is set to true (via the content type form's 'Enable Gutenberg experience' checkbox, or drush cset gutenberg.settings gutenberg_task_enable_full true -y).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Gutenberg-enabled content type 'gutenberg_lock' should have its block template fully locked. Configure Gutenberg so its template lock mode is 'all', and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: gutenberg.settings:gutenberg_lock_template_lock is set to 'all' (drush cset gutenberg.settings gutenberg_lock_template_lock all -y).
